rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement lets a skill link specialized material, but each such link must say when to read the file. I checked each link in the file against that rule:

- **`[CI example](references/ci.md)`**: the text says to use it "when adding these steps to an existing workflow". It also says to check CI when setting up or reviewing a project. This gives the condition.
- **`[references/distributed-requirements.md](...)`**: the text says to read it "before drafting" a requirement that applies separately at many sites, "and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`". This gives the condition.
- **`[references/syntax-details.md](...)`**: the text says to read it "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment ... or a requirement lives in a nested chapter". This gives the condition.
- **`references/fixme.md`**: this is a code-span pointer to another skill's file (the habeas-evidence skill's), not a link. The surrounding sentence already ties it to acknowledging a deferred gap with `{fixme}`. So it has no unconditioned link.

I found no link without a when-to-read statement, so the site has no gap.
